guide.intro: Everything you need to run your first service, in order. Steps tick themselves off as you go.

screens.title: Connect your screens
screens.body: Open Outputs and set your projector or TV to Main output. Only have a laptop? Turn on Rehearsal / window mode to see the output in a small window.

packages.title: Add Bibles and hymnals
packages.body: The King James Version is included. Install other Bible versions (.lsbible) and hymnals (.lshymnal) from files you have been given.

service.title: Build your service
service.body: Pick songs from the Library on the left, verses in the Bible workspace, and media from the bin at the bottom. Double-click (or drag) to put them in the service plan. Drag items to reorder, and use Section to group them.

live.title: Click to go live
live.body: Click a slide and it's on the screen (red). Use {{previous}} / {{next}} to step through slides. Prefer a safety step? Turn on Preview first in the toolbar: clicks go to Preview (green) and {{goLive}} sends them.

control.title: Stay in control
control.body: {{clearContent}} clears the text but keeps the background; {{black}} blacks out the screen; {{panic}} is the panic button that clears everything except the background.

backup.title: Keep your library safe
backup.body: Lampstand backs up daily on its own. Use Export to move your songs, services and media to another computer.

guide.quickBarHelp: Press {{key}} and type a verse, a hymn number or words from a song. Enter shows it (or previews it with Preview first on); Shift+Enter always shows it now.
guide.keysHelp: Change any of them under More › Keyboard shortcuts in the toolbar.

preview.title: Green
preview.body: Preview — ready, not on screen yet.

live.title: Red
live.body: Live — this is on the screen right now.

accent.title: Gold
accent.body: Selected or editable — never affects the screen.

tour.title: Find your way around
tour.help: The window reads left to right: what you have, what you show, what the room sees.

toolbar.title: Toolbar
toolbar.body: Search (or {{quick}}) finds songs, verses and hymns. Show, Edit, Reflow and Bible switch the workspace; Theme opens Themes, and Stage is under More. On the right: the media bin, the Audience and Stage screen lights (green means connected), Preview first, Settings and Status.

sidebar.title: Library and playlists
sidebar.body: The outline at the top lists your libraries (Songs, Hymns) and playlists. Pick one to see its contents underneath: songs to drag in, or the playlist’s items with coloured section bands. Use + to add a song, a playlist or an item.

show.title: Show (the centre)
show.body: The whole playlist on one page, item after item. Click a slide to put it on screen (or into Preview with Preview first on); double-click always goes live; right-click edits it. Switch Grid / Easy (big words) and the slide size at the bottom right.

output.title: Output
output.body: The monitor shows exactly what the room sees. The strip beside it clears one layer at a time (messages, props, slide, media, background); the red power button turns everything off. Below: the Audience or Stage view, and Black (B), Logo (L) and Freeze (F).

controls.title: Show controls
controls.body: Under the monitor: the stage message, timers, messages with fill-in fields, and props. Anything you start here shows on the screens straight away.

media.title: Media bin
media.body: Open it with Media in the toolbar: pictures and videos you import, and the built-in still and motion backgrounds. Click to show, double-click to add to the playlist, or drag onto the slides.

live.title: Going live
live.help: Streaming and recording the service, from the first stream to the low-delay links.

youtube.a:
1. Click Live in the toolbar to open the Live console, then Add under Destinations and pick YouTube or Facebook.
2. In YouTube Studio › Go live › Stream, copy the “Stream key” (the copy button beside the key, not the “Stream URL”). On Facebook: Live video › Streaming software.
3. Paste it into the destination and click Save key. Keys are stored encrypted on this computer and never shown again.
4. Click Go live. The dot beside the destination turns green once the service is receiving.
Any other service that gives you an RTMP address works as Custom RTMP: paste its server address, then its key.

console.a: Live in the toolbar docks the console beside the output; Own window moves it to another display. The picture is exactly what goes out. The top bar shows the frame rate, encoder speed (1.00× keeps up), the sending delay and the computer’s load; the bottom bar shows the bitrate and the encoder. Hover any reading to see what it means. Red or amber readings mean the computer or the internet connection is struggling.

picture.q: Choose what the stream shows and hears
picture.a: In the console, “What the stream shows” sets the words (full screen, a lower third, or none) and what is behind them (the projector’s picture, a camera, or black). Theme draws the lower third in a theme made for it (Stream lower third, Modern lower third, or your own with the Lower third layout). Position puts the lower third left, centre or right; Size fits each slide to the lower third automatically (Auto), or turn Auto off and drag to the size you want. “What the stream hears” picks the channels that go out; the mixer in the Audio tab has a separate stream mix with its own faders. Turn on “Show the stream picture before going live” to check it first.

record.a: Click Record in the Live console: it records with or without streaming. Settings › Streaming can record every time you go live. The file stays playable even if the computer stops unexpectedly.

slow.q: Stream from an older or slower computer
slow.a:
Settings › Streaming › Performance. Click “Check this computer” for a 10-second test, and leave the mode on Auto to use its answer. Light (540p) suits older laptops and slow internet, Balanced (720p) most churches, Quality (1080p) a recent computer with a good upload. If the computer struggles mid-stream, the console offers Switch to Light: a two-second pause, and the stream carries on.
A slow or busy upload is handled by itself: the stream lowers its bitrate to stay live (the bitrate reading turns amber) and climbs back when the connection allows. If the upload stays far too slow for the picture size, the console suggests Light, which looks sharper at that rate. “Check this computer” tests the computer, not the internet: check your upload speed with any speed test (1080p needs about 5 Mb/s, 720p 3, 540p 1.5).

delay.a: Lampstand sends each frame about 0.2 seconds after it is drawn; the console’s delay reading shows this live, and it climbs only if your upload can’t keep up. The rest is added by the streaming service. On YouTube, before going live, open YouTube Studio › Stream settings › Stream latency and pick Ultra low-latency (about 2–5 seconds; Low is 5–10, Normal 15–30). Judge the delay on the public watch page: the preview inside YouTube Studio lags more. For under a second, use a direct link or NDI (below).

direct.q: Send to another room with almost no delay (direct link)
direct.a:
A direct link goes straight to a receiver you run (OBS, vMix, VLC, a decoder box) instead of a service, with well under a second of delay. It can run beside YouTube.
1. On the receiving computer in OBS: add a Media Source, untick “Local file”, and set Input to udp://@:9000. In VLC: Open Network, udp://@:9000, and lower “network caching” in its options.
2. In the Live console, Add › Direct link, and type the receiver’s address with the same port, e.g. udp://192.168.1.50:9000.
3. Go live.
UDP is for the same network. For a link across the internet use SRT (srt://address:9000, with the receiver set to srt://:9000?mode=listener); it resends lost packets, and needs an ffmpeg built with SRT on this computer.

ndi.q: Send to vMix, OBS or NDI gear on the network
ndi.a: Install NDI Tools (free) on this computer, then open Settings › NDI and turn on a feed: the program, the words alone over transparency (to key over cameras), or the stream picture. In vMix, OBS (with the NDI plugin) or NDI Studio Monitor, add an NDI source and pick this computer’s feed by name. NDI stays on the local network and is the lowest-delay way to feed a video mixer.

screens.q: Show a lower third on the projector too
screens.a: Under the output monitor, switch on “Lower third on the screens”. Pick its theme and where it sits (left, centre or right). The audience screens then draw every slide’s words along the bottom in that theme, over a camera or video, until you switch it off; your theme and position are remembered. The stream follows it unless the stream has a theme of its own.

keyFeed.q: Send the words to a video mixer over HDMI (key feed)
keyFeed.a:
1. Plug the mixer into this computer’s HDMI output, open Outputs (the Audience light in the toolbar) and give that display the Alternate role.
2. Under “Alternate output: key feed for a video mixer”, pick Green or Blue (chroma key on the mixer) or Black (luma key). The output then carries only the words and props over that colour.
3. Click “Choose its themes”, pick Lower third, then click a theme and choose Alternate (HDMI), for Scripture, Lyrics and Text.
On an ATEM, use an upstream chroma or luma key with this input as the source. For a clean alpha channel instead, use the NDI “Words” feed.

trouble.q: Fix a stream that won’t start or keeps stopping
trouble.a: A destination that says Stopped shows why when you hover it. “Key needed” or a key that doesn’t look right: copy the Stream key again (not the Stream URL) and save it. Can’t connect: check the internet connection; Lampstand tries YouTube’s second address by itself. An amber bitrate means the upload can’t carry the chosen quality and the stream has lowered itself to stay live; if it stays amber, pick a lighter Performance mode. Picture jumps or readings turn red: the computer can’t keep up, so pick a lighter mode too. Click Retry to bring a stopped destination back without ending the stream.

howto.title: How to…
howto.help: Short recipes for the everyday jobs. Click one to open it.

song.a: Click + next to LIBRARY. Type the words with section headers like [Verse 1] and [Chorus] on their own lines; a blank line starts a new slide. Save, then drag the song onto the playlist, or use its Add to service button.

playlist.a: Click + next to PLAYLISTS. Add sections (Walk-in, Worship, Word…) with the + above the items. On the Show page, fill a section with the “+ Add to …” card at its end (or the + on its coloured band), or drag songs, verses and media onto it. Drag to reorder; a section moves with everything under it, and deleting a section deletes what’s in it. The … beside a playlist’s name duplicates or deletes it.

verse.q: Put a Bible verse on screen
verse.a:
Press {{quick}} and type a reference such as jn 3 16 or Romans 8:28-39. Enter loads Preview, Shift+Enter puts it straight on screen.
In the Bible workspace, clicking a verse opens it in the slides without touching what’s on screen, so it never interrupts a presentation; click the slide to show it, or double-click the verse to show it at once. Turn on “Click shows it now” there if you’d rather a click went straight on screen.

preview.q: Check slides before the room sees them
preview.a: Turn on Preview first in the toolbar. Clicks then load the Preview monitor; press {{goLive}} (or Go live) to send it to the screens.

clear.a: Use the strip beside the monitor to clear one layer, or the red power button ({{clearAll}}) to clear everything. {{panic}} clears the words but keeps the background. Black and Logo cover the screen without losing your place.

backgrounds.a: Open the media bin and pick Backgrounds. Hover a motion background to see it move, click to put it behind your words. Any picture or video in Media can go behind the words too: hover it and click “Use behind the words” (it stays there, under every slide, until you clear the background). Themes can carry a background too.

arrangement.q: Change a song’s order, key or language
arrangement.a: In a song’s header on the Show page, pick an arrangement (a short version, say), transpose the chords for the stage display, or add a translation shown under each line. Write arrangements and translations in the song editor.

edit.a:
Add Slides from the + menu. Click the pencil on a slide card (or open the Edit workspace) to change it: click the words on the canvas to type straight into them, and add text boxes, shapes, lines and pictures. Drag to move, pull the corners to resize. A text item ends with a + card for another slide.
You can edit a slide while it’s live: the screen keeps showing the old version until you press Update live.

import.a: Choose Import in the + menu. PowerPoint comes in as editable text slides; PDF brings each page in as a picture. From Keynote, export to PowerPoint or PDF first.

web.a: Choose Web page in the + menu and enter a secure (https) address. It shows on the audience screens in an isolated view; Black screen covers it.

props.q: Show a logo or notice over everything
props.a: In Show controls › Props, make a prop from a picture or a line of text and click it to show or hide it. Messages show text such as “Parent of {number}” as a lower third or a ticker.

timers.a: Add a Countdown item for a full-screen countdown, or start a timer in Show controls › Timers; running timers show on the stage display.

stage.a: Give a screen the Stage role in Screens (click the Audience or Stage light in the toolbar). It shows the current and next slide, the clock, timers, chords and your stage message.

themes.a: Theme in the toolbar opens Themes. Choose the kind of slide (Scripture, Lyrics, Text) and the layout (Full screen or Lower third), then click a theme and say where to use it: all outputs, or only the main screens, the alternate HDMI output or the stream. The strip at the top shows what each output uses; “Follow main” puts an output back with the main screens. Duplicate a built-in theme to change its fonts, colours, effects and background; Import theme and the export button move themes between computers.

text.q: Change one song’s font or colour
text.a: Select the item in the playlist and press Text in the toolbar. Pick a font, size, bold or italic, colour and alignment; only that item changes, on top of its theme. Use theme puts it back.

logo.q: Set the logo and off-air screen
logo.a: Settings › Presenting: your church name and a tagline on a choice of looks, or your own picture or video. The off-air screen shows it whenever nothing is live.

backup.q: Back up or move your library
backup.a: Settings › Library & backups exports everything (songs, playlists, themes, media) to one file and imports it on another computer. A backup is also made every day.

undo.a: Press {{undo}} (or Edit › Undo in the menu bar) to undo changes to playlists, songs and slides; {{redo}} redoes them.

announcements.a: Add Announcements from the + menu and give each notice its own slide. While live they move on by themselves every few seconds (set the time in the inspector) and loop; turn Loop off in the item to step through them by hand instead.

audio.q: Play music or a video without it starting by itself
audio.a: Clicking a song or sound in Media › Audio selects it; nothing plays until you press its play button (or Play in the room). Videos work the same: put one on screen and press Play, or set Settings › Video › When a video goes live to play straight away.

everything.title: Everything Lampstand does
everything.help: Every feature that works today, by area. Planned ones are listed in Settings › Features.

desk.title: Cameras, sound desks and controllers
desk.help: Switching cameras, bringing in the sound desk, and running Lampstand from a desk or controller over MIDI or OSC.

cameras.a: Media › Sources › Video input lists every camera and capture card. Click one to put it on Preview, then Cut ({{switcherCut}}) or Auto ({{switcherAuto}}) takes it to the screen with the transition chosen beside them (Cut, Fade, Dip or Wipe, and its length); drag the T-bar to mix by hand. Double-click a camera to take it at once. Keys 1–9 preview a camera, Shift+1–9 take it. PiP puts a second camera in a corner. The Switcher button hides Preview and Program when you want bigger cameras. Slide words stay on top of the camera.

deskSound.q: Bring the sound desk into Lampstand
deskSound.a: Connect the desk by USB (or through an audio interface) and install its driver if the maker provides one; many desks need none on a Mac. It then shows in Media › Audio › Audio inputs with a level meter: switch it on and it becomes a channel on the mixer, to the room, the stream or both. Lampstand takes the device’s first two channels, so send the main mix to USB 1–2 on the desk.

midi.q: Run Lampstand from a desk or MIDI controller
midi.a:
1. Plug the desk or controller in by USB (or a MIDI interface). It appears in Settings › Control surfaces under MIDI.
2. Under Controls, choose what a control should do: a show action (next slide, go live, black…), a camera, a mixer fader or mute, or the T-bar.
3. Press Learn, then move the fader or press the button on the desk. Done: it now does that.
The Activity row shows the last control Lampstand heard, to check the connection. Learn again changes a control; the bin removes it.

osc.q: Connect a desk or app over the network (OSC)
osc.a: For desks and apps that speak OSC (TouchOSC, Behringer X32 and Midas M32, many digital desks). In Settings › Control surfaces turn on “OSC over the network”; the page shows this computer’s address and port to type into the desk or app. Enter the desk’s own address and OSC port (an X32 uses 10023) so Lampstand can answer it. Then add controls with Learn as for MIDI. Both computers must be on the same network.

feedback.q: Keep motor faders and button lights in step
feedback.a: Leave “Motor faders and button lights follow” on in Settings › Control surfaces. When you change a fader or a mute in Lampstand, the desk’s motorised fader moves and its button light matches. A fader you’re moving on the desk is left alone, so it never fights your hand.

cues.q: Make the desk react to the show (mute a mic while a video plays)
cues.a: In Settings › Control surfaces › Send to the desk, click Add a cue. Choose when (a video starts or stops, a camera goes on or off, the stream goes live or ends, the screen goes black or is cleared) and the message to send: MIDI (port, CC, note or program change, channel, number, value) or OSC (address and value, e.g. /ch/05/mix/on with 0 to mute channel 5 on an X32). Test sends it now so you can check the desk responds.

deskTrouble.a: Watch the Activity row in Settings › Control surfaces while you move it. Nothing there: for MIDI, check the cable and that the desk shows under MIDI (some desks must be set to send MIDI in their own setup); for OSC, check the port and that the desk points at the address shown, and that a firewall isn’t blocking it. It shows but nothing happens: press Learn for that control again (the desk may send on another channel or number). A Behringer X32 or Midas M32 only sends its own fader moves to apps that keep asking, which Lampstand doesn’t do yet: use its MIDI mode for faders, or OSC to send cues to it.
